Add unrolled functions and unit tests
Add docs page and more tests

fix: implement filter, split, and unique in terms of unrolled_flatmap (#33)

* fix: implement filter, split, and unique in terms of unrolled_flatmap

unrolled_filter, unrolled_split, and unrolled_unique were implemented
as reductions that push items into an accumulator. A pushing reduction
changes the accumulator's type on every step, which triggers Julia
inference's recursion-widening heuristics for long or complexly typed
iterators; the widened accumulator then requires dynamic dispatch and
heap allocation, neither of which can be compiled for GPUs. This broke
ClimaAtmos AMIP runs through ClimaCore's use of unrolled_filter in GPU
kernels (InvalidIRError with gpu_gc_pool_alloc and jl_f__apply_iterate
in unrolled_push_into).

Implement all three functions in terms of unrolled_flatmap, which maps
each item to an empty or singleton iterator based only on that item's
type, so no recursively growing type is inferred. unrolled_unique keeps
an item when no preceding item has the same value of f, which requires
quadratically many comparisons, but the pushing reduction it replaces
also required quadratically many.

Bump the version to 0.1.10.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: pin PrettyTables to v2 for the test and docs table printers

test/test_and_analyze.jl is written against the PrettyTables v2 API
(backend = Val(:html), HtmlDecoration, Crayon highlighters, and v2 text
kwargs), so a fresh resolve of PrettyTables v3 fails the comparison
table printing step at the end of the test suite with a TypeError.
Pin PrettyTables to v2 in the package compat (which governs Pkg.test's
resolution of the test extras) and in docs/Project.toml (which governs
the docs build that renders the same tables).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: precompute cumulative lengths in unrolled_product

The item computations in unrolled_product sliced the iterators with
itrs[1:(itr_index - 1)] inside the ntuple closures, which requires
constant propagation of itr_index to infer each slice's length. On
Julia 1.11, this constant propagation fails, so the slices infer as
Tuple{Vararg} and the index arithmetic becomes dynamic, which fails the
JET type-stability tests on all platforms (and the docbuild, which
renders the same analysis). Precompute the cumulative lengths with
unrolled_cumprod outside the closures, so that each item computation
only needs to index into a homogeneous integer tuple, which is
type-stable for any index.

The full test suite passes on Julia 1.10.10 and 1.11.9 with this
change; on 1.11.9, the released implementation fails the same 16 JET
tests that failed in CI.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: preserve output containers and single predicate evaluation

The flatmap-based implementations of unrolled_filter, unrolled_split,
and unrolled_unique returned plain Tuples for iterators with other
output types: the ConditionalOutputType of a StaticBitVector resolves
against the mapped generator's empty-or-singleton Tuples rather than
the original items, and the unconditional SVector output type would
need to hold the abstract type of those Tuples. Force the intermediate
iterators to be Tuples with unrolled_map_into_tuple, and convert the
results in a single fixed-depth step at the end, into the output type
inferred from the original iterator.

unrolled_split also called f twice per item, contrary to its
documentation, and negated it with !, which requires f to be a
Function and builds a ComposedFunction. Compute the values of f only
once per item into a Tuple of (value, item) pairs and flatten each part
of the split from those pairs.

unrolled_unique compared each item against a StaticOneTo(n - 1) range
whose type is only inferrable when n constant-propagates through the
closure, which cannot be relied on across Julia versions (this is the
pattern that broke unrolled_product on Julia 1.11). Compare against the
full-length range with a guard on the index instead.

Remove the two in-body Base.@assume_effects :foldable annotations in
unrolled_product: they asserted consistency and effect freedom over
closures that read arbitrary user iterators and call user functions,
their original motivation was removed by the cumulative-lengths
rewrite, and heterogeneous products are JET-clean without them on
Julia 1.10 and 1.11 (with identical allocation behavior).

Add test/container_and_callable.jl with the regression tests that
elementwise equality comparisons cannot express: output container
typeof assertions for StaticBitVector, SVector, and MVector (the
StaticArrays extension was previously never loaded in tests; add
StaticArrays to the test target), a call-counting non-Function
predicate for unrolled_split, and JET checks for heterogeneous
products.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: skip output conversion for Tuple results of filter, split, unique

The single-step output conversions added for container preservation
routed Tuple results through unrolled_map_into with identity, whose
extra call layers can prevent the result's value from constant folding
on some Julia versions. Downstream, ClimaCore uses the results of these
functions as type parameters (the names in Components{T, names}), so
the loss of value-level folding on Julia 1.10.11 made
Geometry.product_geometry's return type non-concrete and errored the
FusedMultiBroadcast VIFH test in the downstream CI job. Dispatch the
conversion on the output type and return Tuple results directly, which
restores the exact code path that previously passed downstream while
keeping the conversion for container types like StaticBitVector and
SVector.

Verified: ClimaCore main's unit_field_multi_broadcast_fusion.jl passes
on Julia 1.10.11 with this package dev'd (it reproduced the downstream
failure before this fix), and the container and callable regression
tests pass on Julia 1.10.10, 1.10.11, and 1.11.9.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: assert value-level constant folding for constant inputs

The results of unrolled_filter, unrolled_unique, unrolled_allunique,
unrolled_split, unrolled_take, and unrolled_drop are used as type
parameters downstream (the names in ClimaCore's Components{T, names}),
so their values must constant-fold when their inputs are constant.
Wrapping each result in Val makes inference fail unless the value
folds, and the inputs arrive as type parameters to mirror the
downstream call sites. Even a single additional call layer can break
folding on some Julia versions while leaving results equal and types
stable, so equality tests cannot detect this class of regression.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: add unrolled_flatmap_into and revise selection comments

Define unrolled_flatmap_into(f, output_type, itr) for the shared
pattern in unrolled_filter, unrolled_split, and unrolled_unique, and
revise the surrounding comments to describe the current design and the
failure modes of the alternatives it avoids, without referring to code
that no longer exists.

Verified on Julia 1.10.10, 1.10.11, and 1.11.9: the container and
callable regression tests pass, including the value-foldability
assertions, and ClimaCore main's unit_field_multi_broadcast_fusion.jl
still passes on 1.10.11 with this package dev'd.

test: support CUDA.jl 6 and PrettyTables 3

The comparison-table printer in test/test_and_analyze.jl uses the
PrettyTables 3 API, which CUDATools 6 (a dependency of CUDA.jl 6) requires,
so Project.toml and docs/Project.toml bound PrettyTables to "3". The other
test dependencies have no compat entries, so that developers can test with
newer versions. In test/compilation_limits.jl, the runtime_int helper
converts with unsafe_trunc, which removes the gpu_broken flags, the harness
accepts the print_to_string error that GPUCompiler 2 reports on Julia 1.10,
and LLVM log messages emitted during GPU compilation are discarded, because
logging from inside codegen can deadlock.
